CURRENT STATUS (NOV. 2026): 4 / 10 STEPS COMPLETED · STEP 5 UNDERWAY ↗

svg.text: TIMELINE OF INTERNATIONAL CITIZEN SUBMISSION SEM-26-003
TO PROTECT THE GREAT BOG OF BLAINVILLE AGAINST THE STABLEX EXPANSION
3. PROJECTED STEPS 6 TO 10 (YES / NO · CEC TIMELINES)
Blainville–Stablex agreement (2020), then adverse BAPE ruling on Cell 6 (278,000 m²).
Key finding: Cell 5 capacity is sufficient until 2030, making the expansion premature.
Forced expropriation of lot 6 695 053 (Blainville) and barring of local judicial remedies.
Citizen open letter in Le Devoir (April 8, 2025) denouncing the bypassing of the BAPE.
STEP 1 · MAY 4 → JUNE 3, 2026 (30 D / 30 D): FILED AT AGE 14
1st minor admitted since 1994 (Art. 24.27(1)) · Initial review passed in 30 d, urgent UN
appeal and 5 written notices sent to ECCC/DFO/NRCan (June 3–28, exhibits D01–D12).
STEP 2 · JUNE 29 & JULY 16, 2026 (43 D / 60 D): REVISED & OAG
Petition No. 546 filed with the OAG on June 29 (24 questions, rec’d July 13), then revised
brief in 43 d (15 p. + 102 p., 34 provisions, WaterShed study, 132 bird species, Fauvel Lakes).
STEP 3 · AUG. 17, 2026 (30 D / 30 D): 17 SECTIONS RETAINED
Determination 62/DET: 17 sections retained across 5 laws/reg. (FA, SARA, MBCA, MBR, CEPA —
right to a healthy environment) given “apparent lack of federal inspection” (para. 76).
STEP 4 · OCT. 16–17, 2026 (60 D / 60 D): RESPONSE & REBUTTAL
Ottawa cites Petition 546 (Art. 24.27(4)(a)) to request termination without denying pollution.
7-ground citizen rebuttal filed Oct. 17: an OAG petition (s. 22 AGA) is not a court proceeding.
Mandatory ministerial responses (ECCC / DFO) due on Petition 546 (120 d).
CEC decision (+60 cal. d): recommend (yes) or terminate (no) a factual record.
STEP 6 · ~FEB. 18, 2029 (+796 D AVG. · IF YES): 2/3 COUNCIL VOTE
Vote by at least 2 of 3 ministers (Art. 24.28(2), no statutory cap): observed duration of 617 to
957 d (~Aug. 2028 – July 2029) to instruct (yes) or decline (no) a CEC investigation.
STEP 7 · ~SEPT. 7, 2029 (+201 D AVG. / 120 D): DRAFT RECORD
If instructed: independent CEC scientific and legal investigation and submission of the draft
factual record to Council (statutory cap: 120 calendar d · observed duration: 135 to 240 d).
STEP 8 · ~OCT. 29, 2029 (+52 D AVG. / 30 D): PARTY COMMENTS
Review by Canada, the United States, and Mexico on the factual accuracy of the draft
factual record (USMCA Art. 24.28(5): 30 calendar d allotted · observed: 30 to 69 d).
STEP 9 · ~DEC. 1, 2029 (+33 D AVG. · NO CAP): FINAL RECORD
Secretariat incorporates relevant Party comments and submits the final factual record
to the Ministerial Council (observed real-world duration: 16 to 60 d).
STEP 10 · ~JAN. 14, 2030 (+44 D AVG. / 30 D): PUBLICATION & NGO ACTION
Official publication (~Aug. 2029 – May 2030, matching BAPE’s 2030 capacity horizon) · Prospective
path: partner with environmental NGOs to pursue legal action against the government from CEC findings.
MAY 4, 2040 (+14 YEARS AFTER RECEIPT): LITIGATION & REPARATION
14-year horizon to the day from May 4, 2026 (goal: environmental litigation lawyer): seek
accountability and compensatory damages building on file SEM-26-003, backed by expanded
longitudinal scientific studies and field analyses across the Great Bog of Blainville.
